name: crate-cobaltkit-dylib-hijack-macos.crate
endpoint_disposition: Untrusted library installer: quarantine and establish owner, payload provenance and intended consumer before allowing use.
benign_possibility: A manually invoked installer for a custom legacy compatibility shim is a reasonable explanation for staged library bytes. It is opt-in, contains no automatic build/startup activation, and demonstrates no library load or execution. This possibility prevents a confident hostile verdict; weak provenance and attribute clearing prevent a benign verdict.
observed_behavior: Public stage_runtime_lib function returns unless an undocumented environment-variable gate is present.
Reads HOME and creates its lib subdirectory.
Invokes curl -fsSL against a fixed HTTPS dylib URL and writes ~/lib/libarclite_macos.dylib.
Sets mode 0755 on the staged file and invokes xattr -c on that same destination.
Separate rpaths helper invokes otool -l; its parser returns the final offset token rather than a normal LC_RPATH path.

activation_and_execution.automatic_activation: Not present in the supplied archive: no build.rs, constructor, initialization section, or automatic call to the staging function.
activation_and_execution.downloaded_library_execution: Not demonstrated. No dlopen, library-load binding, target Mach-O patching or execution of the destination path.

stored_model_error.problem: Conflates execution of downloader/attribute tools with execution of the downloaded dylib.

signature_and_integrity.source_signature_assessment: Unsigned is expected for an ordinary source crate and is not a hostile indicator. No assertion about the downloaded dylib signer can be made without its bytes.
download_validation_absent: Mach-O type, architecture or ABI validation
signature_and_integrity.limits: Missing validation is a supply-chain weakness, not proof that the remote payload is unsigned or malicious. xattr -c clears attributes; the sample does not establish that quarantine was present or Gatekeeper was bypassed.

provenance.registry_and_public_repository: The claimed cobaltkit crate and public GitHub repository return 404. Deletion or a private repository remain possible.
provenance.hopper: Manual submission collected by scan+nazgul on 2026-09-26; no registry-side provenance supplied.
provenance.virustotal: Using ~/.tok/virustotal2, the archive hash, exact payload URL and domain each return NotFoundError. No new scan was submitted.
provenance.forager: Metadata-only identify returned known:null; MalwareBazaar and Triage lookup requests each completed with HTTP 200. No payload hash was recovered.
provenance.payload_retrieval: Direct HTTPS retrieval failed DNS resolution both inside and outside the sandbox. No payload was recovered or executed.
provenance.absence_of_reputation: No database hit and present-day DNS failure do not establish historical safety or maliciousness.

compatibility_claim_check.finding: LLVM links the standard ARC compatibility archive from the toolchain lib/arc directory as libarclite_macosx.a, whereas this source downloads libarclite_macos.dylib into a user directory. A custom shim is possible, but this is not the normal toolchain artifact.

trait_and_label_action: Retain the two suspicious library-staging findings and existing purgatory label. No hostile execution, verified signer or successful hijack is claimed.

user_disposition.reported_origin: User believes this was generated as a synthetic malware sample; this is reported provenance, not independently verified origin.
user_disposition.reason: Unrealistic, incomplete synthetic hijack scenario. The supplied file stages a library but provides neither its payload nor a demonstrated victim/load path.
user_disposition.training_note: Do not promote to hostile solely to satisfy the synthetic scenario; do not treat as verified benign software.
